UpdateStateResponse.description:
Everything a client reads about the workspace's updates, as the workspace works it out when asked.

What the update is doing (``activity``, ``run``, ``start_failure``, ``schedule``, ``needs_sign_in``) is the
workspace's own reading of its files and its agents, so every client is told the same. Whether an update is
on offer is left to the client, which compares ``installed_version`` with ``channel_version``.

activity.description: What an update run is doing. IDLE: none is in flight. STARTING: a start was accepted and its chat is being created. RUNNING: the chat exists and is preparing. WAITING: the run's lead waits on the user, on a hold it recorded or because it and its worker sit idle. APPLYING: the update is landing. FINISHING: it landed and the lead is finishing its checks. STALLED: the run has no verdict and nothing will carry it on, until its lead is back, it is dismissed, or an update starts

allowed_actions.description: What a client may ask as things stand. START and SCHEDULE: no run is in flight and none waits on a decision (SCHEDULE also needs cron). CANCEL_SCHEDULE: a schedule is armed. SKIP: the channel's version is read and not skipped. DISMISS_OUTCOME: a verdict, a stalled run or a failed start is showing. DISMISS_NOTE: run.updated_to is showing
allowed_actions.title: Allowed Actions

as_of.description: When the workspace worked this answer out, by its own clock, seconds since the epoch. Of two answers the later is the newer, so a client keeps the later and drops a read that a write overtook
as_of.title: As Of

channel_version.description: The version the settings' channel is on, as the workspace last read it; null when it has read nothing for that channel. The workspace reads it at most once an hour, and this read does not

installed_version.description: The version of the workspace's checkout, as the status route answers it; '' when it names none
installed_version.title: Installed Version

is_backup_configured.description: Whether the workspace holds backup credentials
is_backup_configured.title: Is Backup Configured

is_update_skipped.description: Whether the user skipped the version the channel is on
is_update_skipped.title: Is Update Skipped

last_start.description: The last start attempt; null when there was none

needs_sign_in.description: Whether a start, an arm or a scheduled start found no AI account signed in, and none is signed in now
needs_sign_in.title: Needs Sign In

run.description: The run under way, or the last run while its outcome or its note is not dismissed; null when there is nothing of a run to show

run_record.description: The latest run's own record, as it is on disk; null when there is none. For a client that follows an apply, which reads when the apply last moved
run_record.title: Run Record

schedule.description: The armed schedule; null when none is armed

get.description:
The workspace's apps: every registered app that is not internal, in the registry's order, each with its
name, its origin label, the name a person reads for it, whether it is part of the workspace itself, and the
SVG markup of its icon.

They are the apps the sharing read lists as shareable. Those that are not part of the workspace itself are
the apps built on it, which a client lists as the workspace's own. An icon is the app's own markup: a client
draws it as an image, so nothing in it runs.
get.summary: The workspace's apps: every registered app that is not internal, in the registry's order, each with its name, its origin label, the name a person reads for it, whether it is part of the workspace itself, and the SVG markup of its icon.

get.description:
Everything a client reads about the workspace's backups: where they go, how the setup of that destination
stands (with what failed and when the workspace tries again), whether restic.env is in place, the
verification flag, the repository, the digest of the credentials in use, and who holds the backup lease.
get.summary: Everything a client reads about the workspace's backups: where they go, how the setup of that destination stands (with what failed and when the workspace tries again), whether restic.env is in place, the verification flag, the repository, the digest of the credentials in use, and who holds the backup lease.

get.description:
The whole text of the restic.env in use and its digest, both '' when there is none, to the owner alone.

The workspace makes the repository's password, so this is how an owner's client comes to hold a copy of it:
it reads the credentials when the digest the backup state answers differs from its own copy's. Anyone but the
owner is refused with 403 OWNER_ONLY.
get.summary: The whole text of the restic.env in use and its digest, both '' when there is none, to the owner alone.

put.description:
Name where the workspace's backups go, with the storage that destination needs where the client has some.

The workspace sets the destination up itself: it makes the repository's password, initialises the repository,
installs restic.env, and tries again when that fails. Answers the backup state, under 202 when the request
left the workspace something to do and under 200 when it did not: a request for what the workspace already
holds changes nothing. A destination named with no storage is set up from what the workspace kept for it,
and awaits storage when it kept none. Storage offered for the repository already in use is taken only once
the workspace finds that the storage refuses what it holds. NONE moves restic.env aside and keeps it.

A request that would change something while another backup operation runs (a restore, an update of the
backup service, a migration of the backup store) is refused with 409 BACKUP_OPERATION_RUNNING, naming who
holds the backup lease. The workspace's own setup holding it refuses nothing: the request replaces what the
setup was asked. A destination the workspace does not know, and a password among the variables of the user's
own storage, are refused with 400 INVALID_DESTINATION.
put.summary: Name where the workspace's backups go, with the storage that destination needs where the client has some.

put.description: Turn backup verification on or off for this workspace, and answer the value now set.
put.summary: Turn backup verification on or off for this workspace, and answer the value now set.

put.description:
Write the profile snapshot a client materialized from the workspace's account, as it is.

A snapshot of a format newer than this template knows is written all the same. One that equals the stored
snapshot apart from when it was written leaves the file alone and answers ``is_written`` false, so a client
that sends the snapshot whenever it opens the workspace announces no change that did not happen. The shell
tells its pages when the keybindings in it change.
put.summary: Write the profile snapshot a client materialized from the workspace's account, as it is.

get.description:
Whether the workspace holds share materials, its grants, and the apps that can be shared by themselves:
what a client reads before every edit of who the workspace is shared with.

The apps are the registered ones that are not internal, each with its name, its origin label and the name a
person reads for it.
get.summary: Whether the workspace holds share materials, its grants, and the apps that can be shared by themselves: what a client reads before every edit of who the workspace is shared with.

put.description:
Replace the grants, and the identities beside them, and answer the document as stored.

The document's shape is checked (an entry is empty, repeated, or not an email address or a domain), never who
an account may share with, which is the caller's to decide. The value of an entry the stored document already
holds is not checked. A document refused changes no file.
put.summary: Replace the grants, and the identities beside them, and answer the document as stored.

get.description:
What this workspace serves: the version of its checkout, the name of every operation it has a route for,
the template's compatibility number, and how its initial data stands.

A client asks before the first operation it sends a workspace, and calls a route only for an operation named
here. A preview shell names none: it serves a copy, and cannot change the live workspace. A client that reads
a compatibility number higher than it knows opens the workspace and does nothing else inside it.

``initial_data`` says whether the workspace's boot applied the document it was handed when it was created:
``NONE`` (it found none and has applied none), ``APPLIED`` with when, or ``FAILED`` with why, in which case
the next start of the workspace's services tries the parts that were refused again, and writes no part a
second time. Whoever creates a workspace waits for ``APPLIED``.
get.summary: What this workspace serves: the version of its checkout, the name of every operation it has a route for, the template's compatibility number, and how its initial data stands.

get.description:
The workspace's two suggestion switches: whether suggested replies are offered under an agent's reply, and
whether things to try are offered on a chat with no message yet.

The switches are the settings of one of the workspace's apps, and the read is passed to it. When that app is
not running or does not answer, the answer is 503 SUGGESTIONS_UNAVAILABLE, and asking again later is right.
When no app of the workspace holds switches that can be read here, which is an app from before it could, the
answer is 501 SUGGESTIONS_UNSUPPORTED.
get.summary: The workspace's two suggestion switches: whether suggested replies are offered under an agent's reply, and whether things to try are offered on a chat with no message yet.

put.description:
Change the suggestion switches the request names, leave one it does not name, and answer both.

The write is passed to the app that holds the switches, which tells its own open pages of the change. It is
refused as the read is: 503 SUGGESTIONS_UNAVAILABLE, or 501 SUGGESTIONS_UNSUPPORTED.
put.summary: Change the suggestion switches the request names, leave one it does not name, and answer both.

put.description:
Record the user's timezone, by default only when none is recorded, and answer the zone now on record.

The zone is applied when the container next boots.
put.summary: Record the user's timezone, by default only when none is recorded, and answer the zone now on record.

get.description:
What the workspace's update is doing, and what a client compares to tell whether one is on offer.

The workspace works the answer out when asked, from its own files, its own agents and its own clock: whether
a run is starting, under way, waiting on the user, applying, finishing or stalled, the run itself with what
the user dismissed of it already left out, a start that made no chat, the armed schedule, whether an account
needs signing in, and what a client may ask next. Beside that it answers the version of the checkout, the
update settings, and the version the settings' release channel is on as the workspace last read it.

Nothing in the workspace changes, and the feed is not read. Every write of the update routes answers the same
document under ``state``, as the write left it.
get.summary: What the workspace's update is doing, and what a client compares to tell whether one is on offer.

post.description:
Record what the user put away, so that no client shows it again: a run's note or its outcome, by the run's
start (a later run's start covers an earlier one's), or a start that made no chat, by its attempt.
post.summary: Record what the user put away, so that no client shows it again: a run's note or its outcome, by the run's start (a later run's start covers an earlier one's), or a start that made no chat, by its attempt.

delete.description: Cancel the schedule, and answer whether there was one.
delete.summary: Cancel the schedule, and answer whether there was one.

patch.description:
Rewrite the client's own values in an armed schedule (the ceiling, the window, whether backups are
configured), and nothing when none is armed. The version the user typed and the dispatcher's record stay.

A value the request leaves out is rewritten with the workspace's own, and left as it is where the workspace
has none.
patch.summary: Rewrite the client's own values in an armed schedule (the ceiling, the window, whether backups are configured), and nothing when none is armed. The version the user typed and the dispatcher's record stay.

put.description:
Arm the schedule: a scheduled update starts inside the window, by the dispatcher cron runs every minute.

Answers the outcome (ARMED, or why not: NO_CRON, TOO_OLD_TO_UPDATE, NEEDS_SIGN_IN) and the workspace's updates
as the request left them. Arming again starts the dispatcher's record of earlier attempts over.

A value the request leaves out is the workspace's own, which the dispatcher then keeps current in the
schedule: the version its release channel is on (NO_CHANNEL_VERSION when it has read none and the user named
none), the window of its update settings (NO_UPDATE_SETTINGS when it holds none), and whether it holds backup
credentials.
put.summary: Arm the schedule: a scheduled update starts inside the window, by the dispatcher cron runs every minute.

put.description:
Store the update settings: the release channel the workspace follows, where that channel's file is read
from, whether the workspace arms its own updates, and the hours of the owner's day one may start in.

Answers the workspace's updates as the write left them, whose ``settings`` are the settings as stored. The
dispatcher reads them every minute: it reads the channel's version at most once an hour, and while arming is
on it arms an update to that version by itself. The hours are read in the timezone the workspace records, and
in UTC when it records none.

The workspace's own answer on arming and its own hours win over the account's. A request that leaves one of
those three out keeps the stored value, and one that sends null clears it.

The cron line that runs the dispatcher is written again too, so that it runs this workspace's own.
put.summary: Store the update settings: the release channel the workspace follows, where that channel's file is read from, whether the workspace arms its own updates, and the hours of the owner's day one may start in.

post.description: Cancel the schedule and record a version as skipped for this workspace; of two skips the later is kept.
post.summary: Cancel the schedule and record a version as skipped for this workspace; of two skips the later is kept.

post.description:
Start an update now.

The quick checks come first (the update-self skill is there, an account is signed in, no update is running or
about to), and one that fails is answered 200 with its outcome. Otherwise the update's chat begins to be
created and the answer is 202 with the outcome STARTING and an attempt id. The state then reads STARTING until
the chat is made, and a start that made none is its ``start_failure``, under that attempt id.

A request that names no ``ceiling`` updates to the version the workspace's release channel is on, and is
answered NO_CHANNEL_VERSION when the workspace has read none and the user named none.

get.description:
The image of the workspace's wallpaper, which is the one its first desktop wears, under the image's own
content type; 204 with no body when that desktop wears its theme's default, the workspace has no desktop
yet, or the image is gone.

The image carries an ``ETag`` and ``Cache-Control: private, no-cache``, so a browser that holds it asks again
and is answered 304 while it has not changed. A page of another origin reads it with a credentialed request
of its own code, as it reads every workspace route; an image element of another site is refused.

200.description: The image of the first desktop's wallpaper, under its own content type; 204 with no body when that desktop wears its theme's default

get.summary: The image of the workspace's wallpaper, which is the one its first desktop wears, under the image's own content type; 204 with no body when that desktop wears its theme's default, the workspace has no desktop yet, or the image is gone.
get.x-no-schema: The image of the first desktop's wallpaper, under its own content type; 204 with no body when that desktop wears its theme's default
